text:
maria: Quick bug report - contributors on Poetry editable installs see `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redwood_sdk.asyncio'`. Repro: in sampleapp `poetry install` then `python -c \"import redwood_sdk; import redwood_sdk.asyncio\"` -> import fails, but built wheel from CI contains the subpackages.
sam: Sounds like PEP 660/editable backend oddness. Poetry's editable mode sometimes drops subpackages if package discovery metadata doesn't match. Can you paste pyproject.toml snippet?
maria: Minimal pyproject: `[tool.poetry]
name = "redwood-sdk"
version = "0.0.0"
packages = [ { include = "redwood_sdk" } ]
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = "^3.8"` Layout is standard: `redwood_sdk/__init__.py`, `redwood_sdk/asyncio/__init__.py`, `redwood_sdk/typing/__init__.py`. `pip wheel .` contains subpackages, `poetry install` editable sometimes only installs the root module.
josh: Two quick things: 1) confirm not using implicit namespace packages (PEP 420) - that can confuse installers; 2) check Poetry version (`poetry self show`) - older poetry/core had editable regressions.
maria: We have __init__.py in each subpackage. Not a namespace package.
sam: In the broken env run `python -c \"import redwood_sdk, pkgutil; print(list(pkgutil.walk_packages(redwood_sdk.__path__)))\"` and `pip show -f redwood-sdk` - that'll reveal what files landed on disk.
maria: Done - in poetry env pkgutil lists only the root package and `pip show -f` shows only `redwood_sdk/__init__.py`. In a `pip install -e .` venv everything is present.
dev-bot: CI job #7401 shows unrelated macOS-arm wheel tag error: "ERROR: Invalid wheel tag for platform" (log: https://ci.example/7401)
josh: Practical fix: make packaging explicit in pyproject. Prefer the table form: `
[tool.poetry.packages]
include = "redwood_sdk"
`and add explicit include globs for package files and typing marker, e.g. under `[tool.poetry]` `include = ["redwood_sdk/**", "py.typed"]`. Also `poetry self update` to get latest editable backend fixes.
katie: Short-term workaround for contributors: `pip install -e .` or `poetry build && pip install dist/*.whl`. Long-term: add CI smoke test that does `poetry install` in a clean venv and asserts `import redwood_sdk.asyncio`. I can add a dev doc note about preferring setuptools editable locally.
maria: I'll open a small PR updating pyproject to use explicit `[tool.poetry.packages]`, include `py.typed`, and add a contributing note about editable quirks. Will link PR here when created.
sam: Good. Also add the `pkgutil.walk_packages` snippet to the debugging checklist so others can quickly diagnose.
josh: Agree on CI smoke test + docs. The macOS-arm wheel tag failure looks orthogonal; we'll track it separately.
katie: I'll draft the CI job and dev doc after PR merges. :thumbsup:
maria: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-py/pull/1401 (explicit packages + py.typed + contributing note). Please review.
sam: Reviewing now. Thanks for the concise repro and proposed fix.
